[h1]My Runs[/h1] First game. Started as dwarven healer. By the time I finished my 1st run I used:[list] [*]bullet factories to shoot at enemy with cheep stone walls. [*]steam generators burning healing stone walls with vertical shield projector to block the steam and avoid making water [/list] My 2nd run as dwarven warrior is already:[list] [*]stone wall spam with perk allowing everything to do melee damage [b]and[/b] angry stone perk, while also having extra +5 hp due to another perk. [*]vengeful ant colony which makes enemy regret attacking ants from it. [/list] [strike]Stone walls are rather useful, despite being [i]very[/i] kidnapped-able.[/strike] [h1]About Game[/h1] The game is what it says it is - [b][i]Chaos[/i][/b]. Encounters give [u]you[/u] [i]some[/i] control. The rest is given to [u]enemy[/u] and [u]RNG[/u]. Battles are basically powder toy, [i]but[/i] it is also mana restricted deck builder where individual pixels are actually 25 by 25 pixel-art of creatures, buildings and [i]more[/i]. [h3]Things to worry about before run are:[/h3][list] [*][b]Race[/b] - your beloved classics like [b]dwarf[/b], [b]plant person[/b] or [b]living crystal[/b]. [*][b]Class[/b] - new innovative ideas like [b]healer[/b], [b]warrior[/b] or [b]rouge[/b]. [/list] [h3]Things to worry about during run are:[/h3][list] [*][b]Map[/b] - get to the [b]end[/b] and chose the [b]path[/b] to it. [*][b]Chests and Shops[/b] - get [b]cubes[/b] (basically "cards" of this game) and [b]perks[/b] (basically "perks" of this game). [*][b]Battles[/b] - get [b]gold[/b] and [b][u]not[/u] death[/b]. [*][b]Random Events[/b] - get [b]something[/b] or [b]something[/b] else. [/list] That is the whole gameplay loop at the moment. It is your good old [i]"Easy to learn, but incredibly easy to find funky new synergy, that barely follow laws of physics, if at all."[/i] type of game. I wonder were this will end up with such potential to blow up?.. Hopefully [i]very far[/i] away from my leader; I have too little mana to counter that.

This game is awesome and although I'm writing this as a negative review, I do think there is TONS of fun to have here. However, it's horribly frustrating that once you get to a certain skill level, you will be regularly breaking the game, Noita style. You can reach millions of gold, max and starting mana, and perk stacks that insta-win every battle. Some abilities (I'm looking at you, upgraded bottled universe) even seem to be designed exclusively for God runs, since I don't see any other situation where you could pay 300k for a perk upgrade and survive. The problem is once you hit god status, the game tends to break on a technical level, meaning it slows down to a crawl and eventually crashes. The other issue is that in getting there you will be massively inconvenienced by a UI that simply isn't designed to deal with players who are stacking virtually every perk in the game, some of them hundreds of times. It's no fun getting 1000 consumables and needing to click through each one, or getting 100+ perk choices between battles. Neither is getting 5+ Goblin ball events in a row and being unable to either play or skip them. Want to stop the craziness by voiding your 100 mass bottling plants, 200 reusable bottled perks, etc? Good luck selling or voiding those one at a time, browsing through 10 pages of perks each time. I'm probably going to come back and change this to a positive review at some point because despite the frustration, the game is still awesome most of the time, but I would hope the dev sees this and does something about performance and the UI in late-game. A couple of suggestions would be: - If you're getting lots of stuff, display a one-page summary (ex: Got 123 x Bottled Mana, 15 x Bottled Perk and 259 x Bottled Bees) not individual pickups. - When getting bulk choices, have an "all random button" or even better, allow the player to choose "repeatedly pick this" and maybe "avoid this" and auto-pick where there is only one obvious choice. - Allow bulk selling/voiding perks - Collect metrics for execution times of perk/ability logic and look into those instances where times are through the roof; maybe figure out a way to cap per-frame execution time of any single perk/ability, even if it breaks the logic. Pretty much anything would be better than the save becoming unplayable as it happens now.

Original Review Cube Chaos is an amazing game The main idea is a Sandbox Rogue-Like with massive amounts of variety. You start every run with a few perks and cubes which you can place down on a battlefield during fights for various effects. The main gameplay loop is engaging and not repetitive, with the game offering completely new perks and cubes that you have never seen before basically every run. With this much variety, some balance problems start to arise. Depending on what you get, you can get never-ending god runs within five minutes. The AI isn't very smart or interactive. It gets random cubes every battle, most of which don't do anything for the AI, and sometimes the AI gets a death laser and immediately puts it in front of you with there being little you can't do about it. The amount of luck is tedious at times too; you can spend an entire run looking for the one perk that could save you and never get anything. Despite these issues, the sheer amount of content and playtime in this game is amazing. It is absolutely worth the price. If you love strategy games that you can't take too seriously, or strategy games that you can take very seriously, this is the game for you. Edit: The developer has started addressing a bunch of the issues with the game I stated above by increasing AI intelligence and addressing a bunch of the RNG issues.

I want to like this game, but at this point I feel like I need a compendium or strategy guide since the difficulty does not seem to scale. Early on, random number generation can give the enemy absurd power within seconds of starting while your leader sits there accumulating 1 mana every 10 seconds. There doesn't seem to be the feeling of progression you get with other roguelites - its drudgery, its a grind, and more often than not I leave the game frustrated and looking for something else to play. Strategy takes a back seat in this game, and you are more likely to win by simply re-rolling until you get a game breaking draw.

None of the cards seem to have been created with any sort of foresight or overall strategy in mind. This is more of a totally chaotic sandbox sort of game, rather than a strategic one. Most of the cards are so vague or obtuse in their description that it's impossible to know what it actually does until you've experimented with it. Many of the abilities are also missing tool tips so again, you won't know exactly how it performs until you use it. It might be fun (and rather useless) to have a "gravity distorter" in play, randomly complicating unit movement, but 99% of the time you'll just spawn units until they plod forward and eventually overwhelm the other side. Because there is no deck building (all available cards are random purchases) your strategy just feels like pointless RNG every time.

This game has so much depth and there are so many synergies that I haven't even gone near, even though I've unlocked everything. There's so many cubes, perks and curses and the possibilities are effectively endless. I only have 19 hours of playtime at the time of writing this and can see how someone could easily get at least 200+ hours on this game. And honestly, the variety is half the depth. The other half is how you effectively place those cubes in battle and know when and how to activate certain things. Lastly, here's a few things I did in my short 19 hours: - made an infinite wave of fire from teleporters and self replicating fire waves - made an effectively invincible wall with healing laser launchers shooting at it and time pedestals speeding up the lasers -made a giant mortar wall with armored flies protecting it -died in the first second from starting with too much mana And there's so much I haven't even gotten close to doing. I haven't touched half of my unlocked classes, done even 30% of all the nightmares (self induced difficulty levels), I haven't killed all the bosses yet and in general, I haven't even done from what I can tell, 1/16 of what this game has to offer. Edit: There's also a big active modding community if you ever somehow run out of content

This is a cool idea, but falls short in many respects. While there are many interesting "cubes" with complex behavior, the short battles and roguelike nature mean you will never get a respectable machine going, or at least you certainly can't do so reliably. The reliable strategies that you can replicate from battle to battle and win a run with are one or another kind of "zergling rush": knock out the enemy leader with bullets or ants. Winning strategies rely on a small number of simple, cheap cubes that don't depend on a lot of interactions, which runs contrary to what it feels like the game wants you to do, which to me reflects a poorly realized game concept. The "powerful" "interesting" cubes are locked behind high mana cost and often don't do anything without a lot more expensive setup. You'll never play a run where all opponents allow you that setup. Some of them will, because the enemy AI is fully stupid: "Place random cube in valid position". Some tricky battles (if you haven't found bullets or ants yet) are saved only because the enemy puts a wall in front of the gun they were blitzing you down with. Further discouraging exploration of the game's potential complexity is the fact that the effect descriptions are often pretty rough. "Every 3 seconds, enemy leader, which has manacost greater than 1000, if there is an ally, for every space in each of the four directions around the victim, this cube creates a copy of the cube at position x in your hand, where x is target's column number, divided by 100, except that copy gains Melee: every 2 seconds, do 2 damage to every touching enemy and neutral, and loses this ability." For 100 mana? I'm not even going to read that for 100 mana. No thanks. I'll just rush him down with ants again.

The only two complaints I have are somewhat obtuse UI; and lack of any safeguards, which would prevent the game from freezing when your god run spirals out of control.

This might be the most strategically complex game I've ever played. Seriously. This is a game about trying to either build a basic tower defense and offense of mobile units, or trying to build a Rube Goldberg machine of effects that will eventually win you the level, while being constantly threatened by your computer opponent doing the same. Your strategy of plant soldiers walking across flying giant wurms to attack the enemy boss from above works great until the opponent reverses gravity or drowns you in in sand.
Amazing idea. This should have a sequel with more polish, but even in this raw form is very fun.

Use one cube to make duplicates of another cube placed behind it. The duplicate is dropped to a third cube that turns the duplicate into a cube in my hand that I can place for free. You can animate a rock cube that's normally used as a wall to go forth and fight your enemies. Stack mana regen so high you die instantly. Breathe a sigh of relief when you have a back-up leader. Lose the game because your back-up leader is a chunk of stone that spawned at map gen, sitting right next to the enemy leader. Hurt your own allies to hurt your enemies. Give the cube you're hurting a max health buff that increases over time. Give them 200 health and win the match with one attack on it. There are too many ways to win and many ways to lose in unexpected ways. Finding all the silly ways to win makes this game unique beyond any game I've played. Sometimes it's the one strategy you didn't think would work that turns an impossible match into an easy win. Such a good game.

I don't even know what to say about this game. It's very fun, there are literally infinite strategies you can employ, there are so many cubes I'm finding new ones or at at least new ways to use old ones every single time I open the game, but.... And this is a heavy but... I'm very rarely happy with how things went when I close out. And it's difficult to explain to someone who hasn't played because of how many possibilities there are, but it's like the AI gets to be a baby and do ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and still beat you because it gets so many crutches mid run, especially once you start getting deeper into the challenge mode. I'm leaving this a thumbs up because of how cool the game is, and I want to see more like it. A little word of warning though, you will lose a lot more than you win, and every time it feels bad. But those runs where RNGsus sees fit to bless you with a buttery combos feel so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, it just about makes up for it.
